title: The War Council · Whose Pain?
dek: After Aelthor, the council must find a battlefield and decide what another war may cost. A disputed staff, an ordinary mirror and Aria’s proposed bargain with Death turn the meeting into a struggle over alliances, risk and whose lives can be offered.

facts.People: High Lord Bowene; Aria; Olokun; Scribonia; Jiangshi; Magnus; Míriel; Zarathian commanders
facts.Outcome: Alliance with Death rejected; travel research and war preparations continue

body:
Aelthor had survived the Heavenly Host, but its dead were still shaping the decisions made in Zarathis. At the high war council, the faction representatives and the visiting adventurers faced two problems: how to reach the fighting beyond their shores, and what they were willing to do when they got there.

The meeting on 26 October 2025 did not produce a united vision of that war. It did produce one important refusal. Before Bowene could make it, the people around the table would argue over dangerous travel, Adelia’s staff, the credibility of Magnus’s research and Aria’s suggestion that they ally with Death himself.

A seat at the table

The adventurers were invited to represent the outsiders at the high war council. Seats followed rank. Bowene, Aria, Arandiel, Tarwen, Míriel and the captains gathered in an old room behind green-tinted windows. Magnus waited to speak until those above him had done so. Scribonia, present as a Loremaster, considered when he could properly address the assembly. Jiangshi watched the customs and the quieter reactions around the table.

The building itself enforced a boundary. Jiangshi’s ancestral attendants hesitated, and the ward hurt those who tried to enter. Another attendant collected their clothing and bones. Míriel apologized and offered reimbursement, explaining that undead, celestials and fiends were barred from the secured chamber. Jiangshi acknowledged the mistake and returned to listening.

The first question was practical: how could they find the gods and their armies? Captain Zythienne could train soldiers and prepare weapons, but needed to know the battlefield. Tarwen thought the cosmic war must be fought over another island. Captain Haelith offered to ask the golden beings in Ciaránach, though their answers could be difficult to understand.

What would another war cost?

Arandiel said her forces would be ready, then asked what they might face beyond the servant of the gods they had already fought. Aria answered that the gods were weaker than the others imagined: Fein Uaill had resisted them before. She was more concerned that Death or one of his Knights might be present. Tarwen noticed the change in emphasis and asked why she was suddenly worried about that intervention.

Bowene turned to the outsiders for actual knowledge of other lands. Olokun questioned the whole campaign. They had defended their home against invasion. Why spend its people and resources on a war elsewhere, against enemies whose numbers and strength they did not know? Aria answered that the gods had attacked them in their own land, and Zarathis did not tolerate invasion.

Scribonia added the dangers of the journey itself. In his experience, powerful travelers attracted predators in the Void. He had traveled near its surface, not safely mapped its depths. Moving an army would expose both the soldiers and the mages guiding them. Zythienne suggested a small scouting party first. Míriel could open large Gates once they knew where to go; that knowledge was precisely what they lacked.

None of the proposed methods removed the risk. Scribonia described a previous crossing guided by a Great Void Beast and a tree-linked item, while Plane Shift could move only a small party. Olokun asked about using Gates. Aria said the one she had ordered destroyed on an earlier expedition had led to the hells and would have allowed more demons through. They could discuss routes, but they still had no confirmed destination for the army.

The people behind the equipment

The talk of a traveling staff brought Adelia into the room through other people’s descriptions. Scribonia said she held such an item, but he could not make another: the crude version he had once wielded had not survived his use. Míriel recognized his description of the Great Trees and spoke of the Verdant Circle’s tree in the west. Captain Galathorion offered a contingent to ask for their help.

Bowene offered the treasury in exchange for Adelia lending the artifact. Míriel and Tarwen could offer standing within their orders. Aria turned to Jiangshi, Adelia’s fiancée, to ask what might persuade her. Jiangshi agreed to speak with her after the council and offered her own limited travel magic to help a scouting party and keep a way back open.

Olokun objected to treating Adelia as the obstacle between the council and a useful staff. She had protected their people already. They should ask to work with her, he argued, rather than bargain for her as though she were another resource. Scribonia likewise said she should be consulted and respected. Adelia was absent; the council had not obtained her consent or her staff.

Jiangshi sent a note to tell her what was being requested. The offers remained offers, and the commitments Jiangshi made for herself remained distinct from what Adelia might later choose.

The mirror on the council floor

Magnus offered another possibility. He had been experimenting with water from the Sea of Dreams and wanted to discuss the discovery privately. Aria and Míriel pressed him to explain it in the council instead. Time was short, and they wanted something that could help the expedition now.

He produced a long mirror he said he had created during his experiments. He warned Míriel about its Delerium material before she examined it. She identified and tested it, then gave the plain result: magic had made it, but the finished object was an ordinary mirror. It did not demonstrate a working traveling staff or a new transport for the army.

Magnus argued that more research could produce much greater things. Míriel and other Emerald Veil members were interested. Arandiel was impatient: they had lost too many people to wait on experiments. Olokun answered that useful results still required risk and experimentation. The council wanted immediate certainty from work that had not reached it.

Even after the debate shifted, Magnus continued looking for a way to turn that interest into cooperation with the Veil. His demonstration had drawn attention, but the military problem remained unsolved.

Aria proposes an alliance

Olokun returned to the enemy they were proposing to fight. If they had not reliably defeated even one god, how would they face many? The council was still learning how little it knew when Aria offered a different answer: help Death destroy the gods in exchange for a promise never to touch their realm.

Olokun rose in protest. Death’s forces had already poisoned Gael, Prima and other lands. Why trust a promise from the being responsible? Aria invoked Aelthor’s bereaved families and insisted that an alliance from mortal strength was different from surrendering their souls. Magnus argued that they should at least consider what they could gain if they were going to fight the gods anyway.

Scribonia challenged the proposal on Zarathis’s own terms. A people proud of their independence would risk becoming instruments of Death’s war. They might be offering not just their own lives but their descendants’ lives. Aria insisted on equals rather than slaves. None of those claims produced terms that Death had actually offered or accepted.

Jiangshi could keep her silence no longer. She described her experience near Death’s realm and refused to trade one tyranny for another. She would support the people of Fein Uaill, but not an alliance with him. Aria accepted that refusal while refusing to abandon the war against the gods.

Whose pain can be offered?

The argument became personal. Olokun accused Aria of hiding what had led to Aionia’s attack and of endangering her people through pride. Aria threatened to challenge him in the Rite of Honor. His allegation about the relic did not persuade the council: its acquisition had not been established before those present, and she said the expedition had failed to find it.

Magnus reminded the room that the outsiders were close to clerics of the gods they now proposed to fight. The appeal moved part of the audience. Others remained doubtful about the Void, Death or the plan. Lord-Captain Tyragol appeared more open to the outsiders than most. There was no single, settled Zarathian response to the debate.

Scribonia urged negotiation with the gods before total war. Their individual acts should not automatically condemn every other god, he argued, and destroying their domains could cause further deaths. Tarwen answered that defying the gods was part of Zarathis’s history and identity. Arandiel asked why people who had been attacked and robbed should invite their attackers to tea.

Aria told Olokun she could no longer consider him a friend if he would accept what had happened. He answered that he would fight for their people, but wanted information, a plan and alternatives. When she said pain sometimes had to be endured for victory, he drew the line at choosing who would bear it.

My pain. Not everyone's. I fight so those who can't will be safe. Why do you fight for?Olokun

Aria named a future of safety, security and unbound potential for her people. They could name a similar future without agreeing on what they were entitled to risk to reach it.

Bowene’s decision

Olokun pressed once more against a pact with Death. Bowene answered him directly: they would not pursue that course, if only to retain the adventurers as allies. Olokun sat back in relief, and Jiangshi acknowledged the decision. That was a real result, even though it did not settle the rest of the war.

Magnus was still offering ships, possible contacts and further magical research. Scribonia and Aria continued arguing about the gods and the possibility of repairing the world. Bowene called for quiet and tried to return the council to research on travel and preparation. When the dispute continued, he stopped them all—including Aria—and said he would send orders when ready.

Scribonia agreed to help navigate the Void to save the soldiers’ lives, while refusing to let the disagreement be closed by intimidation. The council ended with a proposed alliance rejected, military preparations continuing, and no completed peace, transport or invasion plan to report.

The next expedition would have to make those choices in practice. When Míriel’s scouts later returned with three possible battlefields, the company would still enter the journey divided over the purpose of the war and the people it meant to protect.
